items.item_text: High school diploma and/or equivalent certification/experience/training.
Bachelor's degree from an accredited university (Preferred)

Manage department records and compile information/data into reports. Maintain and update the department and its auxiliary websites. Coordinate/schedule and facilitate department faculty meetings and other departmental meetings. Create meeting agendas and minutes. Create and disseminate surveys/internal votes and provide data analysis and reports. Manage inventory and equipment for the department. Gather data to assist with course scheduling. Collect and archive syllabi for all courses, and manage desk copy ordering process for graduate students. Take meeting notes that capture deliberations and actions needed for smooth functioning, especially during transitions between chairs. Provide follow-up and track action items from meetings to ensure they are completed. Keep track of dates and deadlines established by the campus. Provide department support with scheduling room reservations and other meeting logistics.

Plan, organize, and implement departmental faculty events, including symposia, conferences, seminars, admissions events, and banquets. Consult with clients on event details and planning. Plan and manage medium to moderately complex events involving guests from multiple locations, such as other public institutions, research institutions, private sector, alumni, and interested donors. Identify potential event locations and vendors. Develop and coordinate guest lists. Perform resource analysis and develop an execution plan, including ensuring funding is available. Ensure compliance with fire marshal and campus policies surrounding events when necessary.

In consultation with Department Services Managers, effectively support department financial processes, review outstanding encumbrances related to Purchase Orders (POs), and consult with requesters to confirm receipt of goods/services, closing POs to release remaining funds. Address "Hold Invoices" by resolving issues like mismatched PO information or vendor discrepancies to ensure prompt processing and posting of expenses within the current fiscal year. During fiscal closure, assist with the accrual process for pending invoices and travel expenses, working with SSHA Finance to confirm that goods/services were received by year-end, and ensure carryforward funds are properly accounted for in the new fiscal year. Support department budget tracking and assist with reconciling accounts. Create and maintain spreadsheets and reports on departmental operations, purchasing, and travel. Handle department purchases on behalf of faculty and provide procurement, reimbursement, and travel support. Provide policy consultation as needed.

Communicate (by email, Zoom, Teams, in person, or by phone) with central offices such as the Academic Personnel Office, Procurement, Space, Web management, Campus Assessment Office, Facilities, IT, Office of the Registrar, Human Resources, etc. The Academic Department Specialist will field questions and connect with appropriate people within the schools and externally to convey information requested by the chair or to determine answers to the faculty and chair's questions. The Academic Department Specialist will advise faculty and department chairs on the campus policies and procedures concerning campus business services and related systems. Manage communications for assigned department(s) and serve as the point of contact for the department(s). Answer questions related to campus business processes and departmental operations from external and internal clients (often researching the questions and/or contacting other offices for clarification on rapidly evolving procedures). Communications may also include calls for information, submission, and collection of materials for a variety of processes.

Personnel Support: Review, collect documentation, and submit Independent Contractor packets to SSHA Academic Personnel; initiate student staff hires, including verification of funding. Collaborate and track submissions of annual requests, i.e., sabbatical leaves, near relative.

Led by the Department Services Manager, implement and maintain efficient local processes. May supervise student staff. The Academic Department Specialist will be the point of contact for their designated departments and will maintain an archive of documents, flyers, brochures, and other related print and digital materials.
